findings.title: Phone header cuts the organisation name and shows only the warehouse code, and neither can be read in full anywhere on the phone
findings.evidence: shell-page__th-mobile-light.png and locale-switch__en-mobile-dark.png header: 'Industrial SAS Loc…' (Thai locale, where the wider 'English' button takes more room) and 'Industrial SAS Local …' (English); second line shows 'LOCAL-DEMO' only. DesktopShell.tsx:209 uses truncate with title={name}, and a title tooltip is unreachable on touch. WorkspaceContextBar.tsx:78 hides the warehouse name below sm. The drawer (shell-drawer__th-mobile-light.png) shows the product name, not the organisation, and the warehouse select is also truncated.
findings.fix: Let the HeaderBrand name wrap to two lines with line-clamp-2 at base size (giving the header a min-height rather than a fixed height), or show the full organisation name as a muted line under the product name in the drawer SidebarHeader, so a phone user can confirm the organisation and warehouse they are working in.

findings.title: Shell loading, navigation-pending and lost-connection states are not in this group

findings.fix: Capture the header skeleton, the navigation-pending indicator after a sidebar click, and the connection notice at 390 and 1440 in both locales.

screens.reachesNineIf: Already at 9 on the captured state; the remaining polish is making the organisation and warehouse name readable in full on the phone.

findings.title: Current-page highlight drops the brand colour in dark mode

The page's own selected tab in dark mode (shell-page__en-mobile-dark.png, 'Products') uses tinted lavender text, so the two selected-state treatments differ on the same screen.
findings.fix: Use the same sidebar-accent token pair for the active row in both themes (tinted primary text and icon on the accent surface), matching the dark-mode selected tab, while keeping the border so selection never depends on colour alone.

findings.title: Warehouse select truncates the Thai warehouse name at 390 px
findings.evidence: shell-drawer__th-mobile-light.png and shell-drawer__en-mobile-dark.png, warehouse select: 'LOCAL-DEMO · คลังทดสอบ Local …'; WorkspaceContextBar.tsx:203 applies truncate to the select value.
findings.fix: Allow the selected value to wrap to two lines inside the select (whitespace-normal, line-clamp-2, min-h-touch instead of a fixed height) so the full warehouse name is readable in the drawer.

screens.reachesNineIf: Use one active-row treatment in both themes so the drawer's selected state matches the rest of the dark UI.

findings.title: Outlined search button in the rail looks like a selected destination

findings.fix: In collapsed mode, render the search trigger as a borderless ghost icon button (like the other rail icons) and keep the border plus accent fill exclusively for the aria-current item.

findings.title: Warehouse switcher and 'Buildings & spots' use near-identical building glyphs in the rail

findings.title: Rail tooltips and submenu behaviour are not captured

findings.title: On desktop, the AI scope and approved disclosure copy is set at 12 px muted text, small for Thai with stacked tone marks
findings.evidence: search-empty__th-desktop-light.png, 'ให้ AI พาไป' note under the heading (y≈503), one ~600 px line of 12 px grey Thai; search-empty--recents__en-desktop-dark.png y≈539-555; SearchDialog.tsx:672 group note uses 'px-2 pb-1 text-xs text-muted'. findings.title: Employee results for a code prefix are not in code order: EMP-DEMO-001 is listed third
findings.evidence: search-results--mixed__th-mobile-light.png and search-results--mixed__en-desktop-dark.png, Employees (4) group: EMP-DEMO-002, EMP-DEMO-003, EMP-DEMO-001, EMP-VIDEO-004. The server sorts by match rank then code (convex/hr/search.ts:100-104), but the client merges review hits before admin hits into a Map and never re-sorts (src/components/shell/search/results.tsx:443-445), so a member with both permissions sees review-scope people first.
findings.fix: After merging reviewItems and adminItems in results.tsx, sort employees.values() with the server's comparator (match rank, then code.localeCompare) before building choices, and add a GlobalSearch test with overlapping review/admin hits that expects code order.
findings.benchmark: Linear search: exact and prefix ID matches rank predictably at the top

findings.title: The same Latin query returns a different task set in Thai than in English

findings.fix: Product owner: decide whether English aliases should cover the words of every English label, so a Thai-locale member typing an English term finds the same destinations. If yes, add 'review employee day' to hr.task.reviewDay aliases and a registry test that every English label is matchable from the Thai locale.

notes: I read all 12 images as pixels. The shell is consistent across 390 and 1440 px and across both locales and themes. The header names the organisation, the sidebar names the product (D3), the language button shows the target language in its own script with lang set and a hidden 'switch to' prefix (LocaleSwitcher.tsx), and the theme toggle shows the current theme with aria-pressed. Phone header controls and drawer rows use the 48px touch token (globals.css:58). The drawer shows an aria-hidden overflow chevron when more destinations sit below. Thai tone marks and vowels are unclipped in the header, sidebar, drawer and page title. axe is clean in every capture and no page overflows. Cross-screen issues: (1) the active navigation row uses a blue tint in light mode but neutral grey in dark mode, filed on shell-drawer; (2) organisation and warehouse names are truncated on the phone with no place to read them in full, filed on shell-page. The global search dialog is not in this group, so I made no search-dialog findings. Runtime QA reports passing checks for Back/Close focus return, collapsed-rail persistence across refresh and locale change, and Escape behaviour; I did not lower any score for interactive behaviour (D9).

All 12 images were read as pixels. No Thai clipping was visible in any capture: tone marks in ตั้งวันหยุด, ลืมลงเวลาเมื่อวาน, บุคลากร, ไม่ใช้งาน and the highlighted สมชาย sit clear of their row bounds. Thai wraps at word boundaries in the AI note on 390 px. Mobile uses a full-screen sheet with about 48 px rows and a 48 px input, desktop a 672 px dialog with 36 px rows and a keyboard hint footer that switches from 'Esc ปิด' to 'Esc ล้าง' once text is typed. Match highlighting is bold plus colour, so it does not rely on colour alone. The selected row uses a tint plus a left accent bar in both themes. Cross-screen: the 12 px muted ASK note (SearchDialog.tsx:672) affects both screens on desktop, and I filed it on both because it shows in both captured states. Disclosure: while searching source for the reviewDay alias, one grep result line surfaced text from docs/plans/ui-improvement-loop-2026-11-04/stages/s1/audits/loop-9-audit-opus.json. I did not open that file or read further. I had already noticed the Thai/English task-count difference in the images (no count beside งานที่ทำได้ versus 'Tasks (2)'), and I verified the cause myself in src/lib/navigation.ts:454-468.

All 12 images were read as pixels. Search no-match follows D14/D16: the AI row comes first with the query echoed, the scope sentence and disclosure, then a 'Go to' fallback list ordered by the current module (D15). The desktop footer states the keyboard contract, and runtime-qa.json confirms Escape clears then closes and focus returns on close. The AI running state replaces the row with a spinner, a 'reading your request' status and a 48 px Cancel on the phone. Typed results stay above it, and the match is highlighted in both locales: in the title in Thai, and as a 'Matches “pallets”' detail in English. The shell-loading state keeps the page title and card layout, gives a reason, says it retries automatically and offers one Reload action. Its weakness is the waiting text repeated across the header, sidebar and card. In dark mode, active and pending AI rows use a neutral grey fill, while light mode uses a blue tint. That difference shows on both search screens and is filed on search-no-match. Thai copy wraps at word boundaries with no clipped tone marks in any capture. The 12 px muted detail lines match the design-system metadata size.

Inspected all 10 images as pixels. Both screens follow the cross-cutting error anchor: each says why the page failed, says that saved data is safe, and gives one primary next step. The route error adds a secondary destination the member can open (Go to Finished goods) and a copyable reference with page and time. Thai renders without clipped tone marks or vowels in headings, buttons, the Notice, or the reference row. Primary buttons are 48 CSS px on phones and 36 px on desktop, as the dense variant sets them. There is no page overflow and axe is clean on every capture. The not-found page renders outside the signed-in shell with only the wordmark, language and theme controls, and its neutral 'Go to start page' follows D11. The two screens differ on purpose (a page header with a summary for not-found, a danger Notice for the route error), and both share the PageHeader type scale and the max-w-xl/2xl column. The only visible shared-component defect is the off-centre idle Retry label from the hidden spinner in PageFailure.tsx, which every route-error capture shows. The retrying state (#10) keeps the button width and adds a spinner with 'Trying again…', and the copied state (#9) swaps to a check icon with 'คัดลอกแล้ว' plus an sr-only status. Both are good feedback.
